notes: Now consider non-felicitous (130a) and felicitous (130b). In both the noun bulcut ‘hunter’ has been turned into a property and can modify the noun kihi ‘person’. In both examples the second, negated bulcut appears on top of bulcut kihi ‘hunter person’. In (130a) the form of negation betrays the adjectival (property) status of the upper bulcut. Hence we get a contradiction – ‘a person who is A but not A’ leading to unacceptability. In (130b), on the other hand, we have the buolbatax-negation which is interpreted, by default, as negating a noun58. What we get in (130b), then, is perfectly interpretable: ‘a person who is A but not N’.
en: a hunting person (with hunter-like qualities) without hunting (hunter-like) qualities
